You are an adversarial verifier for a proposed STRUCTURAL refactor in the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim.
READ-ONLY: do not edit, build, or run anything. Use Read/Grep/Glob only.

Claim (from reviewer scripts):
- file: scripts/run_e2e.sh:8
- category: stale-doc
- title: Header says VSIM_BIN defaults to 'first sim_* under $VSIM_BIN_DIR' but the code pins sim_ax45mpv_premium
- detail: The env-override doc at line 8 states the VSIM_BIN default is 'first sim_* under $VSIM_BIN_DIR'. The code (lines 32-43) deliberately defaults to $VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax45mpv_premium (the canonical single-hart engine, with an 11-line comment explaining why first-sim_* is wrong on multicore builds like sim_ax45mpv_mp2) and only falls back to the first sim_* when the canonical engine is not built. The header contradicts the carefully-chosen behavior directly below it; a reader trusting line 8 would expect sim_ax45mpv_mp2 to be picked on a box where it sorts first.
- claimed safety: Comment-only change (rewrite line 8 to 'default: sim_ax45mpv_premium, falling back to the first sim_*'). No executable line is touched.

Try to REFUTE it. For dead-code: grep the WHOLE repo (and the demo suite at /home/nick/work/andesim-demo, and consider that vsim lives in a separate repo /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim - grep there too if the symbol could cross repos) for references. For duplication: read both sites fully and check they really are behavior-identical. For stale-doc: read the doc AND the code it describes. For bug-report: check whether the behavior is actually wrong vs intended. If the change could alter ANY observable behavior (output text, exit codes, file layout, test expectations), verdict RISKY with the exact risk. If the claim is wrong, REJECTED. Only CONFIRMED when you verified the evidence yourself.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.

- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Run the hybrid e2e tests. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts
3	# (source ./setup.sh first to export the external qemu/vsim locations).
4	#
5	# Env overrides:
6	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64)
7	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
8	#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: first sim_* under $VSIM_BIN_DIR)
9	#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
10	#   MODE         marker | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
11	#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
12	#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
13	#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
14	#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
15	#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
16	#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
17	#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
18	#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
19	#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)
20	
21	set -euo pipefail
22	
23	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
24	# vsim sim_* live in the external VSIM_BIN_DIR (setup.sh exports it, mirroring
25	# VSIM_QEMU); empty when setup.sh has not run -- the require below reports it.
26	VSIM_BUILD="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}"
27	HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
28	TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"
29	
30	VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
31	VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
32	if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
33	  # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andesim
34	  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
35	  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under $VSIM_BIN_DIR -- the
36	  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
37	  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
38	  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
39	  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
40	  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
41	    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_BUILD"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
42	  fi
43	fi
44	
45	step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
46	ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
47	warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
48	fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
49	
50	require() {
51	  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
52	    fail "$1 not found: $2"
53	    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
54	    exit 1
55	  fi
56	}
57	require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
58	require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
59	require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"
60
